flag: US: keep hiring records (applications, resumes, notes) for at least 1 year, and all relevant records once a charge is filed. Harper never advises deleting records.
US: several states and cities ban asking about salary history; Harper never asks for or records past pay anywhere in the process.
Section 503 record-keeping still applies (2 years for 150+ employees or a $150k+ contract, 1 year otherwise); EO 11246 duties under 41 CFR 60-1.12 end when the rescission takes effect on 2026-10-26.
US background checks: FCRA disclosure and authorisation first; before declining anyone on a report, the pre-adverse and adverse-action steps apply. A plain rejection email is never used for this.
New York City: an automated tool that substantially assists screening may need a bias audit no older than 1 year, a public summary, and candidate notice 10 business days before use (Local Law 144).
Illinois: HB 3773 (in force 2026) requires notice when AI is used in hiring decisions, bars discriminatory effect, and names ZIP code as a proxy.
Illinois: AI analysis of video interviews needs notice, an explanation and consent, and deletion within 30 days of the applicant's request (AI Video Interview Act).
US: several other states and cities (for example New York, Washington, Illinois) also require a pay range in postings; this checklist covers only CA and CO; ask the people lead which apply.
California: employers with 15 or more employees must put a good-faith pay scale in postings and must not seek salary history (Labor Code 432.3).
California: FEHA automated-decision rules (from 2025-10-01) can make vendors liable as agents and require keeping automated-decision records for 4 years.

Colorado: SB 26-189 (effective 2027-01-01) replaced the stayed 2024 AI Act: notice before automated decision-making technology is used in a consequential decision such as hiring, a disclosure after an adverse outcome, and records kept for at least 3 years.
Colorado: postings need pay as a closed range, a general description of benefits, and how and when to apply; 'open until filled' is not enough.
EU: AI used in recruitment or selection is high-risk under the AI Act (Annex III 4(a)); the high-risk obligations apply from 2027-12-02 under Regulation (EU) 2026/1744.
EU: GDPR Art. 22 restricts decisions based solely on automated processing; a named person must make each decision.
EU: inferring emotion from video or voice in the workplace, hiring included, is prohibited under the AI Act.

UK: under UK GDPR Arts. 22A-22D (as amended by the Data (Use and Access) Act 2025, in force 2026-02-05) a significant decision with no meaningful human involvement needs safeguards (information, a way to contest, human review); one based on special-category data is restricted.
UK: no health or disability questions before an offer, except in narrow cases (Equality Act 2010 s.60).
UK: keep recruitment records no longer than needed and tell candidates before keeping them in a talent pool (ICO guidance).
